This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

timezone_offset.caption: Timezone Offset
timezone_offset.description: The number of minutes that the reported event time is ahead or behind UTC, in the range -1,080 to +1,080. This allows consumers to reconstruct the local time at the event source. For example, US Eastern Standard Time is -300. Populate this when the source provides local time zone information.

type_name.caption: Type Name
type_name.description: The event/finding type name, combining the class and activity (e.g., "Detection Finding: Create"). The value must match the class_name and activity_name joined by ": ".

type_uid.caption: Type ID
type_uid.description: The event/finding type ID. It identifies the event's semantics and structure. Producers and mappers must compute this as class_uid * 100 + activity_id. It uniquely identifies the combination of event class and activity across the entire schema. For example, Detection Finding: Create is 200401.

unmapped.caption: Unmapped Data
unmapped.description:
A container for source-specific attributes that do not map to any defined OCSF attribute. Use this to preserve valuable source data that would otherwise be lost during normalization. The keys and values are specific to the event source.

Note: Consumers should not rely on a stable structure within this field. The preferred approach to unmapped attributes is to create a custom extension with the desired structure.

win_service.caption: Windows Service
win_service.description: The current Windows service. On failed or unknown status of Reconfigure action may be populated with the intended state.

access_level.caption: Access Level
access_level.description: The generalized access level or permission scope granted to the identity through the analyzed policy configuration. Common examples include Read, Write, List, Delete, Admin, or custom permission levels.

access_type.caption: Access Type
access_type.description: The type or category of access being granted to the identity. This describes the nature of the access relationship, such as cross-account access, public access, federated access, or third-party integration access. Examples include 'Cross-Account', 'Public', 'Federated', 'Service-to-Service', etc.

accessors.caption: Accessors
accessors.description: The identities that are granted access through the analyzed policy configuration. This identifies the specific entity that can exercise the permissions and helps assess the access relationship and potential security implications. Examples include user accounts, service principals, roles, account identifiers, or system identities.

additional_restrictions.caption: Additional Restrictions
additional_restrictions.description: Details about supplementary restrictions and guardrails that may limit the granted access, applied through additional policy types such as Resource Control Policies (RCPs) and Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS, or other policy constraints.

condition_keys.caption: Condition Keys
condition_keys.description: The condition keys and their values that constrain when and how the granted access can be exercised. These conditions define the circumstances under which the access relationship is valid and the privileges can be used. Examples: IP address restrictions like 'aws:SourceIp:192.0.2.0/24', time-based constraints like 'aws:RequestedRegion:us-east-1', MFA requirements like 'aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent:true', or custom conditions based on resource tags and request context.

granted_privileges.caption: Granted Privileges
granted_privileges.description: The specific privileges, actions, or permissions that are granted through the analyzed access relationship. This includes the actual operations that the accessor can perform on the target resource. Examples: AWS actions like 'sts:AssumeRole', 's3:GetObject', 'ec2:DescribeInstances'; Azure actions like 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/read'; or GCP permissions like 'storage.objects.get'.

is_disabled.caption: Disabled
is_disabled.description: Indicates if the account is disabled.

is_locked.caption: Locked
is_locked.description: Indicates if the account is locked. For example, due to the amount of failed logins.

is_on_premises_sync_enabled.caption: On-Premises Sync Enabled
is_on_premises_sync_enabled.description: Indicates whether synchronization with an on-premises directory service is enabled. For example, Microsoft Entra Connect.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the account.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the account (e.g. GCP Project name , Linux Account name or AWS Account name).

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the account.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The account type, normalized to the caption of 'account_type_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized account type identifier.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the account (e.g. AWS Account ID , OCID , GCP Project ID , Azure Subscription ID , Google Workspace Customer ID , or M365 Tenant UID).

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

app_name.caption: Application Name
app_name.description: The client application or service that initiated the activity. This can be in conjunction with the user if present. Note that app_name is distinct from the process if present.

app_uid.caption: Application ID
app_uid.description: The unique identifier of the client application or service that initiated the activity. This can be in conjunction with the user if present. Note that app_name is distinct from the process.pid or process.uid if present.

application.caption: Application
application.description: The client application or service that initiated the activity. This can be in conjunction with the user if present. Note that application is distinct from the process if present.

authorizations.caption: Authorization Information
authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

iam_role.caption: IAM Role
iam_role.description: The actor's role, or as an alternative to user or process when the role is serving as a security principal for the operation that initiated the activity.

idp.caption: Identity Provider
idp.description: This object describes details about the Identity Provider used.

invoked_by.caption: Invoked by
invoked_by.description: The name of the service that invoked the activity as described in the event.

process.caption: Process
process.description: The process that initiated the activity.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The user session from which the activity was initiated.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user that initiated the activity or the user context from which the activity was initiated.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Detailed information about the policy document that defines this restriction, including policy metadata, type, scope, and the specific rules or conditions that implement the access control.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The current status of the policy restriction, normalized to the caption of the status_id enum value.

status_id.caption: Status ID
status_id.description: The normalized status identifier indicating the applicability of this policy restriction.

classification.caption: Classification
classification.description: The vendors classification of the Advisory.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the Advisory record was created.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the Advisory record was created.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A brief description of the Advisory Record.

install_state.caption: Install State
install_state.description: The install state of the Advisory.

install_state_id.caption: Install State ID
install_state_id.description: The normalized install state ID of the Advisory.

is_superseded.caption: The patch is superseded.
is_superseded.description: The Advisory has been replaced by another.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the Advisory record was last updated.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The time when the Advisory record was last updated.

os.caption: OS
os.description: The operating system the Advisory applies to.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product where the vulnerability was discovered.

references.caption: References
references.description: A list of reference URLs with additional information about the vulnerabilities disclosed in the Advisory.

related_cves.caption: Related CVEs
related_cves.description: A list of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) identifiers related to the vulnerabilities disclosed in the Advisory.

related_cwes.caption: Related CWEs
related_cwes.description: A list of Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) identifiers related to the vulnerabilities disclosed in the Advisory.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size in bytes for the Advisory. Usually populated for a KB Article patch.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The Advisory link from the source vendor.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the Advisory.

uid.caption: Advisory ID
uid.description: The unique identifier assigned to the advisory or disclosed vulnerability, e.g, GHSA-5mrr-rgp6-x4gr.

end_column.caption: End Column
end_column.description: The column number of the last part of the assessed code identified as vulnerable.

end_line.caption: End Line
end_line.description: The line number of the last line of code block identified as vulnerable.

file.caption: File
file.description: Details about the file that contains the affected code block.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: Details about the user that owns the affected file.

remediation.caption: Remediation Guidance
remediation.description: Describes the recommended remediation steps to address identified issue(s).

rule.caption: Related Rule
rule.description: Details about the specific rule, e.g., those defined as part of a larger policy, that triggered the finding.

start_column.caption: Start Column
start_column.description: The column number of the first part of the assessed code identified as vulnerable.

start_line.caption: Start Line
start_line.description: The line number of the first line of code block identified as vulnerable.

architecture.caption: Architecture
architecture.description: Architecture is a shorthand name describing the type of computer hardware the packaged software is meant to run on.

cpe_name.caption: The product CPE identifier
cpe_name.description: The Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) name. For example: cpe:/a:apple:safari:16.2.

epoch.caption: Epoch
epoch.description: The software package epoch. Epoch is a way to define weighted dependencies based on version numbers.

fixed_in_version.caption: Fixed In Version
fixed_in_version.description: The software package version in which a reported vulnerability was patched/fixed.

hash.caption: Hash
hash.description: Cryptographic hash to identify the binary instance of a software component. This can include any component such file, package, or library.

license.caption: Software License
license.description: The software license applied to this package.

license_url.caption: Software License URL
license_url.description: The URL pointing to the license applied on package or software. This is typically a LICENSE.md file within a repository.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The software package name.

package_manager.caption: Package Manager
package_manager.description: The software packager manager utilized to manage a package on a system, e.g. npm, yum, dpkg etc.

package_manager_url.caption: Package Manager URL
package_manager_url.description: The URL of the package or library at the package manager, or the specific URL or URI of an internal package manager link such as AWS CodeArtifact or Artifactory.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The installation path of the affected package.

purl.caption: Package URL
purl.description: A purl is a URL string used to identify and locate a software package in a mostly universal and uniform way across programming languages, package managers, packaging conventions, tools, APIs and databases.

release.caption: Software Release Details
release.description: Release is the number of times a version of the software has been packaged.

remediation.caption: Remediation Guidance
remediation.description: Describes the recommended remediation steps to address identified issue(s).

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The link to the specific library or package such as within GitHub, this is different from the link to the package manager where the library or package is hosted.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of software package, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type of software package.

uid.caption: Package UID
uid.description: A unique identifier for the package or library reported by the source tool. E.g., the libId within the sbom field of an OX Security Issue or the SPDX components.*.bom-ref.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor who published the software package.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The software package version.

name.caption: Agent Name
name.description: The name of the agent or sensor. For example: AWS SSM Agent.

policies.caption: Agent Policies
policies.description: Describes the various policies that may be applied or enforced by an agent or sensor. E.g., Conditional Access, prevention, auto-update, tamper protection, destination configuration, etc.

type.caption: Agent Type
type.description: The normalized caption of the type_id value for the agent or sensor. In the case of 'Other' or 'Unknown', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized representation of an agent or sensor. E.g., EDR, vulnerability management, APM, backup & recovery, etc.

uid.caption: Agent ID
uid.description: The UID of the agent or sensor, sometimes known as a Sensor ID or aid.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate Agent ID
uid_alt.description: An alternative or contextual identifier for the agent or sensor, such as a configuration, organization, or license UID.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The company or author who created the agent or sensor. For example: Crowdstrike.

version.caption: Agent Version
version.description: The semantic version of the agent or sensor, e.g., 7.101.50.0.

ai_model.caption: AI Model
ai_model.description: The AI model backing this agent at the time of the recorded event. An agent's model may change across instances or versions; this captures the model in use for the specific logged activity or delegation.

charter.caption: Agent Charter
charter.description: A document that defines an AI agent's durable role, responsibilities, constraints, and operating boundaries. When available, populate hashes on the file for content integrity and signatures for provenance. Integrity of the event that reports this agent is provided separately by the record_integrity profile.

instance_uid.caption: AI Agent Instance ID
instance_uid.description: Identifier for a specific running instance or session of the agent, distinct from the stable logical uid. An instance is a single materialization of the agent: a conversation, session, or run. It may persist across restarts (a session that is suspended and later resumed keeps the same instance_uid) and may span multiple cooperating runtime components, so several events can share one instance_uid. Enables attribution of actions to a particular instance of the agent rather than to the agent generally.

name.caption: Name
name.description: Human-readable name for the agent. For example: Q4 Analysis Agent or Model Tester Agent.

type.caption: Agent Type
type.description: The agent framework, normalized to the caption of the type_id value.

type_id.caption: Agent Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized identifier for the agent framework. Different agent frameworks have different identity, tool-call, and delegation semantics, so recording the framework enables cross-framework normalization. Communication protocols (e.g., MCP, A2A) are a property of individual operations rather than the agent itself, and are surfaced on the relevant operation rather than here.

uid.caption: AI Agent ID
uid.description: The stable logical identifier for the agent, assigned by the agent's authoritative source (e.g., its control plane, registry, or issuing identity provider). Persists across restarts and instances. Producers populate this from whatever identity they observe: for a runtime that owns the agent, this is its issued ID; for a gateway or proxy, it is typically derived from the agent's credential. Multiple producers logging the same agent should converge on the same uid when they share an authoritative source.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

version.caption: AI Agent Version
version.description: The version of the agent: the agent's own code or configuration revision (e.g., 1.4.2), distinct from the version of the model backing it (carried on ai_model.version). Enables correlation of behavioral changes with charter or configuration revisions across agent versions.

ai_provider.caption: AI Provider
ai_provider.description: AI service provider or organization name. For example: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or Internal.

name.caption: Name
name.description: Human-readable model name. For example: gpt-4o, claude-3-sonnet, or text-embedding-ada-002.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the AI model.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

version.caption: Version
version.description: Model version identifier. For example: 2024-05-13, v2.1.0, or beta.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The detailed geographical location usually associated with an IP address.

model.caption: Model
model.description: The model name of the aircraft or unmanned system.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the aircraft, such as the such as the flight name or callsign.

serial_number.caption: Serial Number
serial_number.description: The serial number of the aircraft.

speed.caption: Speed
speed.description: Ground speed of flight. This value is provided in meters per second with a minimum resolution of 0.25 m/s. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: 255 m/s.

speed_accuracy.caption: Speed Accuracy
speed_accuracy.description: Provides quality/containment on horizontal ground speed. Measured in meters/second.

track_direction.caption: Track Direction
track_direction.description: Direction of flight expressed as a “True North-based” ground track angle. This value is provided in clockwise degrees with a minimum resolution of 1 degree. If aircraft is not moving horizontally, use the “Unknown” value

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The primary identification identifier for an aircraft, such as the 24-bit International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) identifier of the aircraft, as 6 hex digits.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: A secondary identification identifier for an aircraft, such as the 4-digit squawk (octal representation).

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

vertical_speed.caption: Vertical Speed
vertical_speed.description: Vertical speed upward relative to the WGS-84 datum, measured in meters per second. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: 63 m/s.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The specific name or identifier of the analysis target, such as the username of a User Account, the name of a Kubernetes Cluster, the identifier of a Network Namespace, or the name of an Application Component.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The category of the analysis target, such as User Account, Kubernetes Cluster, Network Namespace, or Application Component.

algorithm.caption: Algorithm
algorithm.description: The algorithm used by the underlying analytic to generate the finding.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the analytic that generated the finding.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the analytic that generated the finding.

related_analytics.caption: Related Analytics
related_analytics.description: Other analytics related to this analytic.

sensor_info_list.caption: Sensor Information List
sensor_info_list.description: An array of sensor_info objects, each describing a sensor control point analyzed or correlated by the analytic. Each element typically represents a source of related_events that contributed to the finding. An individual sensor control point may also directly originate the finding, though more commonly it emits alerts that a downstream consumer treats as findings.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The analytic type.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The analytic type ID.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the analytic that generated the finding.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The analytic version. For example: 1.1.

observation_parameter.caption: Observation Parameter
observation_parameter.description: The specific parameter, metric or property where the anomaly was observed. Examples include: CPU usage percentage, API response time in milliseconds, HTTP error rate, memory utilization, network latency, transaction volume, etc. This helps identify the exact aspect of the system exhibiting anomalous behavior.

observation_type.caption: Observation Type
observation_type.description: The type of analysis methodology used to detect the anomaly. This indicates how the anomaly was identified through different analytical approaches. Common types include: Frequency Analysis, Time Pattern Analysis, Volume Analysis, Sequence Analysis, Distribution Analysis, etc.

observations.caption: Observations
observations.description: Details about the observed anomaly or observations that were flagged as anomalous compared to expected baseline behavior.

observed_pattern.caption: Observed Pattern
observed_pattern.description: The specific pattern identified within the observation type. For Frequency Analysis, this could be 'FREQUENT', 'INFREQUENT', 'RARE', or 'UNSEEN'. For Time Pattern Analysis, this could be 'BUSINESS_HOURS', 'OFF_HOURS', or 'UNUSUAL_TIME'. For Volume Analysis, this could be 'NORMAL_VOLUME', 'HIGH_VOLUME', or 'SURGE'. The pattern values are specific to each observation type and indicate how the observed behavior relates to the baseline.

analysis_targets.caption: Analysis Targets
analysis_targets.description: The analysis targets define the scope of monitored activities, specifying what entities, systems or processes are analyzed for activity patterns.

anomalies.caption: Anomalies
anomalies.description: List of detected activities that significantly deviate from the established baselines. This can include unusual access patterns, unexpected user-agents, abnormal API usage, suspicious traffic spikes, unauthorized access attempts, and other activities that may indicate potential security threats or system issues.

baselines.caption: Baselines
baselines.description: List of established patterns representing normal activity that serve as reference points for anomaly detection. This includes typical user interaction patterns like common user-agents, expected API access frequencies and patterns, standard resource utilization levels, and regular traffic flows. These baselines help establish what constitutes 'normal' activity in the system.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The information pertaining to the API group.

request.caption: API Request Details
request.description: Details pertaining to the API request.

response.caption: API Response Details
response.description: Details pertaining to the API response.

service.caption: Service
service.description: The information pertaining to the API service.

token.caption: Token
token.description: The API or client token used to authenticate or authorize the API request. This attribute contains the base token object that represents: (1) IdP-issued client tokens (type_id: 6) such as Okta API tokens or Microsoft Entra ID Application Registration client secrets, or (2) generic API tokens/keys (type_id: 7) used for SaaS application authentication. Use this attribute when the API request was authenticated using a token that should be tracked as part of the API activity event. Note: Protocol-specific authentication tokens (Kerberos, OIDC, SAML) should be represented using authentication_token in authentication events, not in API activity events.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the API service.

criticality.caption: Business Criticality
criticality.description: The criticality of the application as defined by the event source.

desc.caption: Application Description
desc.description: A description or commentary for an application, usually retrieved from an upstream system.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The name of the related application or associated resource group.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified name of the application.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the application.

name.caption: Application Name
name.description: The name of the application.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the application.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The software product that this application is an instance of, carrying product identity such as vendor_name, cpe_name, and canonical version.

region.caption: Region
region.description: The cloud region of the resource.

resource_relationship.caption: Application Relationship
resource_relationship.description: A graph representation showing how this application relates to and interacts with other entities in the environment. This can include parent/child relationships, dependencies, or other connections.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

sbom.caption: Related SBOM
sbom.description: The Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) associated with the application

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the application.

type.caption: Application Type
type.description: The type of application as defined by the event source, e.g., GitHub, Azure Logic App, or Amazon Elastic BeanStalk.

uid.caption: Application ID
uid.description: The unique identifier for the application.

uid_alt.caption: Application Alternative ID
uid_alt.description: An alternative or contextual identifier for the application, such as a configuration, organization, or license UID.

version.caption: Application Version
version.description: The semantic version of the application, e.g., 1.7.4.

category.caption: Category
category.description: The category that the assessment is part of. For example: Prevention or Windows 10.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the assessment criteria, or a description of the specific configuration or signal the assessment is targeting.

meets_criteria.caption: Meets Criteria
meets_criteria.description: Determines whether the assessment against the specific configuration or signal meets the assessments criteria. For example, if the assessment checks if a Datastore is encrypted or not, having encryption would be evaluated as true.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the configuration or signal being assessed. For example: Kernel Mode Code Integrity (KMCI) or publicAccessibilityState.

policy.caption: Assessment Policy
policy.description: The details of any policy associated with an assessment.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the configuration or signal being assessed. For example: the signal_id.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

mitigation.caption: MITRE Mitigation
mitigation.description: The Mitigation object describes the MITRE ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Mitigation ID and/or name that is associated to an attack.

sub_technique.caption: MITRE Sub-technique
sub_technique.description: The Sub-technique object describes the MITRE ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Sub-technique ID and/or name associated to an attack.

tactic.caption: MITRE Tactic
tactic.description: The Tactic object describes the Tactic ID and/or name associated to an attack.

tactics.caption: Tactics
tactics.description: The Tactics associated with the attack technique.

technique.caption: MITRE Technique
technique.description: The Technique object describes the MITRE ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Technique ID and/or name associated to an attack.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Matrix version.

authority_uid.caption: Authority ID
authority_uid.description: Unique identifier of the authority that produced this attestation. When the attestation has a signature, authority_uid ties the signing credential to a known party: because signing credentials rotate and expire, a verifier uses this identifier to confirm that the credential belongs to the expected authority, rather than to a different holder of some otherwise-valid credential. Where multiple signatures are present, it identifies the authority that produced the attestation; the identity of each co-signer is carried within its own digital_signature object. Included in the canonical serialization.

chain_uid.caption: Chain ID
chain_uid.description: Identifier of the append-only chain, such as a forensic or audit log, that this event belongs to. It groups a sequence of attestations so that an independent verifier can locate and validate them in order; it identifies the chain itself and is not a reference to any event outside of this one. Stable for the lifetime of the chain. For example, every attestation produced during a single agent session shares one chain_uid, so querying events whose attestation.chain_uid matches retrieves the full chain, including its newest entry, while each event links to its predecessor through prev_event.

fingerprint.caption: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of this event's canonical serialization. If signatures are present, each signature is computed over this fingerprint. Without signatures, the fingerprint alone still detects accidental alteration or corruption of the event. The next event in a chain references this value through its own prev_event.fingerprint.

prev_event.caption: Previous Event
prev_event.description: Reference to the previous event in a tamper-evident chain, carrying that event's fingerprint together with locator attributes for retrieval. Absent on the first, or genesis, event of a chain.

signatures.caption: Digital Signatures
signatures.description: One or more digital signatures, each computed over this event's fingerprint and thereby over the event's canonical serialization, each bound to a verifiable identity. The first entry is typically the producer; additional entries carry co-signatures such as a notary or witness over the same event. The signing algorithm, certificate or public-key material, and signing time are carried within each digital_signature object.

uid.caption: Attestation ID
uid.description: Unique identifier of this attestation. It distinguishes an individual attestation, such as a single entry within a tamper-evident chain, from the chain as a whole. See chain_uid for the identifier of the chain itself.

device.caption: Device
device.description: Device used to complete an authentication request.

email_addr.caption: Email Address
email_addr.description: The email address used in an email-based authentication factor.

factor_type.caption: Factor Type
factor_type.description: The type of authentication factor used in an authentication attempt.

factor_type_id.caption: Factor Type ID
factor_type_id.description: The normalized identifier for the authentication factor.

is_hotp.caption: HMAC-based One-time Password (HOTP)
is_hotp.description: Whether the authentication factor is an HMAC-based One-time Password (HOTP).

is_totp.caption: Time-based One-time Password (TOTP)
is_totp.description: Whether the authentication factor is a Time-based One-time Password (TOTP).

phone_number.caption: Phone Number
phone_number.description: The phone number used for a telephony-based authentication request.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The name of provider for an authentication factor.

security_questions.caption: Security Questions
security_questions.description: The question(s) provided to user for a question-based authentication factor.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time that the authentication token was created or issued. This corresponds to the token issuance time, such as the iat (issued at) claim in OIDC tokens, the issue instant in SAML assertions, or the ticket start time in Kerberos tickets.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time that the authentication token was created or issued. This corresponds to the token issuance time, such as the iat (issued at) claim in OIDC tokens, the issue instant in SAML assertions, or the ticket start time in Kerberos tickets.

encryption_details.caption: Encryption Details
encryption_details.description: The encryption details of the authentication token.

expiration_time.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time.description: The expiration time of the authentication token.

expiration_time_dt.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time_dt.description: The expiration time of the authentication token.

is_renewable.caption: Renewable
is_renewable.description: Indicates whether the authentication token is renewable.

kerberos_flags.caption: Kerberos Flags
kerberos_flags.description: A bitmask, either in hexadecimal or decimal form, which encodes various attributes or permissions associated with a Kerberos ticket. These flags delineate specific characteristics of the ticket, such as its renewability or forwardability.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The last time the token was updated.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The last time the token was updated.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The human-friendly name of a token or key, if available, such as the name from the Okta API Token API.

tenant_uid.caption: Tenant UID
tenant_uid.description: The unique identifier of the tenant or organization that owns the token or key, or the tenant context in which the token is authorized for use. This is particularly relevant in multi-tenant Identity Provider scenarios where tokens are scoped to specific tenants.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the authentication token.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized authentication token type identifier. This attribute restricts the base token.type_id enum to only protocol-specific authentication token types (values 0, 1-5, 99). API tokens and client tokens (values 6-7) are not valid for authentication_token - use the base token object for those types.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique ID of a token or key, if available, such as the Secret ID of Entra ID Application Registration Client Secrets.

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or geographic region that the token or key is authorized to be used from. This may represent network-based access restrictions, geographic limitations, or other zone-based authorization policies. Examples include Okta's network zone restrictions or cloud provider region restrictions.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Details about the Identity/Access management policies that are applicable.

name.caption: Name
name.description: Organization name for the Autonomous System.

number.caption: Number
number.description: Unique number that the AS is identified by.

observation_parameter.caption: Observation Parameter
observation_parameter.description: The specific parameter or property being monitored. Examples include: CPU usage percentage, API response time in milliseconds, HTTP error rate, memory utilization, network latency, transaction volume, etc.

observation_type.caption: Observation Type
observation_type.description: The type of analysis being performed to establish baseline behavior. Common types include: Frequency Analysis, Time Pattern Analysis, Volume Analysis, Sequence Analysis, Distribution Analysis, etc.

observations.caption: Observations
observations.description: Collection of actual measured values, data points and observations recorded for this baseline.

observed_pattern.caption: Observed Pattern
observed_pattern.description: The specific pattern identified within the observation type. For Frequency Analysis, this could be 'FREQUENT', 'INFREQUENT', 'RARE', or 'UNSEEN'. For Time Pattern Analysis, this could be 'BUSINESS_HOURS', 'OFF_HOURS', or 'UNUSUAL_TIME'. For Volume Analysis, this could be 'NORMAL_VOLUME', 'HIGH_VOLUME', or 'SURGE'. The pattern values are specific to each observation type and indicate the baseline behavior.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of a specific campaign associated with a cyber threat.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the certificate was created.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the certificate was created.

expiration_time.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time.description: The expiration time of the certificate.

expiration_time_dt.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time_dt.description: The expiration time of the certificate.

fingerprints.caption: Fingerprints
fingerprints.description: The fingerprint list of the certificate.

is_self_signed.caption: Certificate Self-Signed
is_self_signed.description: Denotes whether a digital certificate is self-signed or signed by a known certificate authority (CA).

sans.caption: Subject Alternative Names
sans.description: The list of subject alternative names that are secured by a specific certificate.

serial_number.caption: Certificate Serial Number
serial_number.description: The serial number of the certificate used to create the digital signature.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the certificate.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The certificate version.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The detailed description of the compliance check, explaining the security requirement, vulnerability, or configuration being assessed. For example, CIS: The cramfs filesystem type is a compressed read-only Linux filesystem. Removing support for unneeded filesystem types reduces the local attack surface. or DISA STIG: Unauthorized access to the information system by foreign entities may result in loss or compromise of data.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name or title of the compliance check. For example, CIS: Ensure mounting of cramfs filesystems is disabled or DISA STIG: The Ubuntu operating system must implement DoD-approved encryption to protect the confidentiality of remote access sessions.

resource.caption: Resource
resource.description: Describes details about the resource that this check evaluated.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The severity level as defined in the source document. For example CIS Benchmarks, valid values are: Level 1 (security-forward, essential settings), Level 2 (security-focused environment, more restrictive), or Scored/Not Scored (whether compliance can be automatically checked). For DISA STIG, valid values are: CAT I (maps to severity_id 5/Critical), CAT II (maps to severity_id 4/High), or CAT III (maps to severity_id 3/Medium).

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description: The normalized severity identifier that maps severity levels to standard severity levels. For example CIS Benchmark: Level 2 maps to 4 (High), Level 1 maps to 3 (Medium). For DISA STIG: CAT I maps to 5 (Critical), CAT II maps to 4 (High), and CAT III maps to 3 (Medium).

standards.caption: Compliance Standards: List
standards.description: The regulatory or industry standard this check is associated with. E.g., PCI DSS 3.2.1, HIPAA Security Rule, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, or ISO/IEC 27001:2013.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The resultant status of the compliance check normalized to the caption of the status_id value. For example, CIS Benchmark: Pass when all requirements are met, Fail when requirements are not met, or DISA STIG: NotAFinding (maps to status_id 1/Pass), Open (maps to status_id 3/Fail).

status_id.caption: Status ID
status_id.description: The normalized status identifier of the compliance check.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the compliance check within its standard or framework. For example, CIS Benchmark identifier 1.1.1.1, DISA STIG identifier V-230234, or NIST control identifier AC-17(2).

version.caption: Version
version.description: The check version. For example, CIS Benchmark: 1.1.0 for Amazon Linux 2 or DISA STIG: V2R1 for Windows 10.

cis_controls.caption: CIS Controls
cis_controls.description: The CIS Critical Security Controls is a prioritized set of actions to protect your organization and data from cyber-attack vectors.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The CIS Benchmark description. For example: The cramfs filesystem type is a compressed read-only Linux filesystem embedded in small footprint systems. A cramfs image can be used without having to first decompress the image.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The CIS Benchmark name. For example: Ensure mounting of cramfs filesystems is disabled.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The CIS benchmark description.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The CIS benchmark name.

remediation.caption: Remediation Guidance
remediation.description: Describes the recommended remediation steps to address identified issue(s).

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The CIS Control description. For example: Uninstall or disable unnecessary services on enterprise assets and software, such as an unused file sharing service, web application module, or service function.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The CIS Control name. For example: 4.8 Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The CIS Control version. For example: v8.

control.caption: Security Control
control.description: A Control is prescriptive, prioritized, and simplified set of best practices that one can use to strengthen their cybersecurity posture. e.g. AWS SecurityHub Controls, CIS Controls.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The CIS critical security control version.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the classifier.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the classifier.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the classifier.

contents.caption: Clipboard Contents
contents.description: The data items written to, or read from, the clipboard.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the clipboard on systems with named clipboards. For example: General or Drag.

binary_data.caption: Binary Data
binary_data.description: The item's data in binary form, used when the clipboard content cannot be represented as text or when preserving the exact binary representation is required.

clipboard_native_type.caption: Data Type
clipboard_native_type.description: The type of the item's data, in an operating specific form. For example: CF_TEXT or public.utf8-plain-text.

mime_type.caption: MIME type
mime_type.description: The Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (MIME) type of the item's data. For example: text/plain.

string_data.caption: String Data
string_data.description: The item's data if it can be represented as a UTF-8 string.

account.caption: Account
account.description:
The Account object containing details about the cloud account, subscription, or billing unit where the event or finding was created. This object includes properties such as the account name, unique identifier, type, labels, and tags.

Examples:
  • AWS: Account object with name, uid (Account ID), type, and other account properties
  • Azure: Subscription object with name, uid (Subscription ID), type, and subscription metadata
  • GCP: Project object with name, uid (Project ID), type, and project attributes
  • Oracle Cloud: Compartment object with name, uid (Tenancy OCID), type, and compartment details

cloud_partition.caption: Cloud Partition
cloud_partition.description:
The logical grouping or isolated segment within a cloud provider's infrastructure where the event or finding was created, often used for compliance, governance, or regional separation.

Examples:
  • AWS: Partition where the event occurred (aws, aws-cn, aws-us-gov)
  • Azure: Cloud environment where the event occurred (AzureCloud, AzureUSGovernment, AzureChinaCloud)

org.caption: Organization
org.description:
The Organization object containing details about the organizational unit or management structure that governs the account, subscription, or project where the event or finding was created. This object includes properties such as the organization name, unique identifier, type, and other organizational metadata.

Examples:
  • AWS: Organization object with name, uid (Organization ID), type, and other organizational properties
  • Azure: Management Group object with name, uid (Management Group ID), type, and management group metadata
  • GCP: Organization object with name, uid (Organization ID), type, and organizational attributes
  • Oracle Cloud: Tenancy object with name, uid (Tenancy OCID), type, and tenancy details

project_uid.caption: Project ID
project_uid.description: The unique identifier of a Cloud project.

provider.caption: Cloud Provider
provider.description: The unique name of the Cloud services provider where the event or finding was created. Examples include AWS, Azure, GCP (Google Cloud Platform), Oracle Cloud, IBM Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, or other public, private, or hybrid cloud providers.

region.caption: Region
region.description:
The cloud region where the event or finding was created, as defined by the cloud provider.

Examples:
  • AWS: Region where the event occurred (us-east-1, eu-west-1)
  • Azure: Region where the event occurred (East US, West Europe)
  • GCP: Region where the event occurred (us-central1, europe-west1)
  • Oracle Cloud: Region where the event occurred (us-ashburn-1, uk-london-1)

zone.caption: Cloud Availability Zone
zone.description:
The availability zone in the cloud region where the event or finding was created, as defined by the cloud provider.

Examples:
  • AWS: Availability zone where the event occurred (us-east-1a, us-east-1b)
  • Azure: Availability zone where the event occurred (1, 2, 3 within a region)
  • GCP: Availability zone where the event occurred (us-central1-a, us-central1-b)
  • Oracle Cloud: Availability zone where the event occurred (AD-1, AD-2, AD-3)

assessments.caption: Assessments
assessments.description: A list of assessments associated with the compliance requirements evaluation.

category.caption: Category
category.description: The category a control framework pertains to, as reported by the source tool, such as Asset Management or Risk Assessment.

checks.caption: Compliance Checks
checks.description: A list of compliance checks associated with specific industry standards or frameworks. Each check represents an individual rule or requirement that has been evaluated against a target device. Checks typically include details such as the check name (e.g., CIS: 'Ensure mounting of cramfs filesystems is disabled' or DISA STIG descriptive titles), unique identifiers (such as CIS identifier '1.1.1.1' or DISA STIG identifier 'V-230234'), descriptions (detailed explanations of security requirements or vulnerability discussions), and version information.

compliance_references.caption: Compliance Standard References
compliance_references.description: A list of reference KB articles that provide information to help organizations understand, interpret, and implement compliance standards. They provide guidance, best practices, and examples.

compliance_standards.caption: Compliance Standards: Details
compliance_standards.description: A list of established guidelines or criteria that define specific requirements an organization must follow.

control.caption: Security Control
control.description: A Control is a prescriptive, actionable set of specifications that strengthens device posture. The control specifies required security measures, while the specific implementation values are defined in control_parameters. E.g., CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark 1.2.0 - Control 2.1 - Ensure CloudTrail is enabled in all regions

control_parameters.caption: Control Parameters
control_parameters.description: The list of control parameters evaluated in a Compliance check. E.g., parameters for CloudTrail configuration might include multiRegionTrailEnabled: true, logFileValidationEnabled: true, and requiredRegions: [us-east-1, us-west-2]

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description or criteria of a control.

requirements.caption: Compliance Requirements
requirements.description: The specific compliance requirements being evaluated. E.g., PCI DSS Requirement 8.2.3 - Passwords must meet minimum complexity requirements or HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(a)(2)(iv) - Implement encryption and decryption mechanisms

standards.caption: Compliance Standards: List
standards.description: The regulatory or industry standards being evaluated for compliance.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The resultant status of the compliance check normalized to the caption of the status_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

status_code.caption: Status Code
status_code.description: The resultant status code of the compliance check.

status_detail.caption: Status Detail
status_detail.description: The contextual description of the status, status_code values.

status_details.caption: Status Details
status_details.description: A list of contextual descriptions of the status, status_code values.

status_id.caption: Status ID
status_id.description: The normalized status identifier of the compliance check.

hash.caption: Hash
hash.description: Commit hash of image created for docker or the SHA256 hash of the container. For example: 13550340a8681c84c861aac2e5b440161c2b33a3e4f302ac680ca5b686de48de.

image.caption: Image
image.description: The container image used as a template to run the container.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the container.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The container name.

network_driver.caption: Network Driver
network_driver.description: The network driver used by the container. For example, bridge, overlay, host, none, etc.

orchestrator.caption: Orchestrator
orchestrator.description: The orchestrator managing the container, such as ECS, EKS, K8s, or OpenShift.

pod_uuid.caption: Pod UUID
pod_uuid.description: The unique identifier of the pod (or equivalent) that the container is executing on.

runtime.caption: Runtime
runtime.description: The backend running the container, such as containerd or cri-o.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size of the container image.

tag.caption: Image Tag
tag.description: The tag used by the container. It can indicate version, format, OS.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the container.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The full container unique identifier for this instantiation of the container. For example: ac2ea168264a08f9aaca0dfc82ff3551418dfd22d02b713142a6843caa2f61bf.

cores.caption: Cores
cores.description: The number of processing cores or compute units for the component.

cpu_architecture.caption: CPU Architecture
cpu_architecture.description: The CPU architecture, normalized to the caption of the cpu_architecture_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the source.

cpu_architecture_id.caption: CPU Architecture ID
cpu_architecture_id.description: The normalized identifier of the CPU architecture.

cpu_bits.caption: CPU Bits
cpu_bits.description: The number of bits used by the CPU for memory addressing.

model.caption: Model
model.description: The model name of the CPU. For example: Intel Xeon Gold 6348, AMD EPYC 7763, or Apple M3 Max.

speed_mhz.caption: Compute Unit Speed (MHz)
speed_mhz.description: The nominal clock speed of the unit, expressed in megahertz.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor of the CPU. For example: Intel, AMD, or Apple.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The Record Creation Date identifies when the CVE ID was issued to a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) or the CVE Record was published on the CVE List. Note that the Record Creation Date does not necessarily indicate when this vulnerability was discovered, shared with the affected vendor, publicly disclosed, or updated in CVE.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The Record Creation Date identifies when the CVE ID was issued to a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) or the CVE Record was published on the CVE List. Note that the Record Creation Date does not necessarily indicate when this vulnerability was discovered, shared with the affected vendor, publicly disclosed, or updated in CVE.

cvss.caption: CVSS Score
cvss.description: The CVSS object details Common Vulnerability Scoring System scores from the advisory that are related to the vulnerability.

cwe.caption: CWE
cwe.description: The CWE object represents a weakness in a software system that can be exploited by a threat actor to perform an attack. The CWE object is based on the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) catalog.

cwe_uid.caption: CWE UID
cwe_uid.description: The Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) unique identifier. For example: CWE-787.

cwe_url.caption: CWE URL
cwe_url.description: Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) definition URL. For example: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/787.html.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A brief description of the CVE Record.

epss.caption: EPSS
epss.description: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) object describes the estimated probability a vulnerability will be exploited. EPSS is a community-driven effort to combine descriptive information about vulnerabilities (CVEs) with evidence of actual exploitation in-the-wild.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The Record Modified Date identifies when the CVE record was last updated.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The Record Modified Date identifies when the CVE record was last updated.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product where the vulnerability was discovered.

references.caption: References
references.description: A list of reference URLs with additional information about the CVE Record.

related_cwes.caption: Related CWEs
related_cwes.description: Describes the Common Weakness Enumeration details related to the CVE Record.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the CVE record.

type.caption: Vulnerability Type
type.description:
The vulnerability type as classified in the CVE catalog.

Most frequently used vulnerability types are: DoS, Code Execution, Overflow, Memory Corruption, Sql Injection, XSS, Directory Traversal, Http Response Splitting, Bypass something, Gain Information, Gain Privileges, CSRF, File Inclusion. For more information see Vulnerabilities By Type distributions.

uid.caption: CVE ID
uid.description: The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures unique number assigned to a specific computer vulnerability. A CVE Identifier begins with 4 digits representing the year followed by a sequence of digits that acts as a unique identifier. For example: CVE-2021-12345.

base_score.caption: Base Score
base_score.description: The CVSS base score. For example: 9.1.

depth.caption: CVSS Depth
depth.description: The CVSS depth represents a depth of the equation used to calculate CVSS score.

metrics.caption: Metrics
metrics.description: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System metrics. This attribute contains information on the CVE's impact. If the CVE has been analyzed, this attribute will contain any CVSSv2 or CVSSv3 information associated with the vulnerability. For example: { {"Access Vector", "Network"}, {"Access Complexity", "Low"}, ...}.

overall_score.caption: Overall Score
overall_score.description: The CVSS overall score, impacted by base, temporal, and environmental metrics. For example: 9.1.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description:
The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) Qualitative Severity Rating. A textual representation of the numeric score.

CVSS v2.0
  • Low (0.0 – 3.9)
  • Medium (4.0 – 6.9)
  • High (7.0 – 10.0)

CVSS v3.0
  • None (0.0)
  • Low (0.1 - 3.9)
  • Medium (4.0 - 6.9)
  • High (7.0 - 8.9)
  • Critical (9.0 - 10.0)

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The source URL for the CVSS score. For example: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-44228

vector_string.caption: Vector String
vector_string.description: The CVSS vector string is a text representation of a set of CVSS metrics. It is commonly used to record or transfer CVSS metric information in a concise form. For example: 3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The vendor that provided the CVSS score. For example: NVD, REDHAT etc.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The CVSS version. For example: 3.1.

caption.caption: Caption
caption.description: The caption assigned to the Common Weakness Enumeration unique identifier.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: URL pointing to the CWE Specification. For more information see CWE.

uid.caption: CWE ID
uid.description: The Common Weakness Enumeration unique number assigned to a specific weakness. A CWE Identifier begins "CWE" followed by a sequence of digits that acts as a unique identifier. For example: CWE-123.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The tactic name that is associated with the defensive technique. For example: Isolate.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The versioned permalink of the defensive tactic. For example: https://d3fend.mitre.org/tactic/d3f:Isolate/

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the defensive tactic.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the defensive technique. For example: IO Port Restriction.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The versioned permalink of the defensive technique. For example: https://d3fend.mitre.org/technique/d3f:IOPortRestriction/

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the defensive technique. For example: D3-IOPR.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

d3f_tactic.caption: MITRE D3FEND™ Tactic
d3f_tactic.description: The Tactic object describes the tactic ID and/or name that is associated with a countermeasure.

d3f_technique.caption: MITRE D3FEND™ Technique
d3f_technique.description: The Technique object describes the technique ID and/or name associated with a countermeasure.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The D3FEND™ Matrix version.

category.caption: Category
category.description: The name of the data classification category that data matched into, e.g. Financial, Personal, Governmental, etc.

category_id.caption: Category ID
category_id.description: The normalized identifier of the data classification category.

classifier_details.caption: Classifier Details
classifier_details.description: Describes details about the classifier used for data classification.

confidentiality.caption: Confidentiality
confidentiality.description: The file content confidentiality, normalized to the confidentiality_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

confidentiality_id.caption: Confidentiality ID
confidentiality_id.description: The normalized identifier of the file content confidentiality indicator.

discovery_details.caption: Discovery Details
discovery_details.description: Details about the data discovered by classification job.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Details about the data policy that governs data handling and security measures related to classification.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The source URL pointing towards the full classification job details.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The resultant status of the classification job normalized to the caption of the status_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

status_details.caption: Status Details
status_details.description: The contextual description of the status, status_id value.

status_id.caption: Status ID
status_id.description: The normalized status identifier of the classification job.

total.caption: Total
total.description: The total count of discovered entities, by the classification job.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the classification job.

category.caption: Category
category.description: The name of the data classification category that data matched into, e.g. Financial, Personal, Governmental, etc.

category_id.caption: Category ID
category_id.description: The normalized identifier of the data classification category.

classifier_details.caption: Classifier Details
classifier_details.description: Describes details about the classifier used for data classification.

confidentiality.caption: Confidentiality
confidentiality.description: The file content confidentiality, normalized to the confidentiality_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

confidentiality_id.caption: Confidentiality ID
confidentiality_id.description: The normalized identifier of the file content confidentiality indicator.

data_lifecycle_state.caption: Data Lifecycle State
data_lifecycle_state.description: The name of the stage or state that the data was in. E.g., Data-at-Rest, Data-in-Transit, etc.

data_lifecycle_state_id.caption: Data Lifecycle State ID
data_lifecycle_state_id.description: The stage or state that the data was in when it was assessed or scanned by a data security tool.

detection_pattern.caption: Detection Pattern
detection_pattern.description: Specific pattern, algorithm, fingerprint, or model used for detection.

detection_system.caption: Detection System
detection_system.description: The data security tool or system that the finding, detection, or alert originated from, normalized to the caption of detection_system_id. E.g., Endpoint, Secure Email Gateway, etc.

detection_system_id.caption: Detection System ID
detection_system_id.description: The normalized identifier of the data security tool or system type from which the finding, detection, or alert originated. When the type is not listed, use 99 (Other) and populate detection_system with the source-specific label.

discovery_details.caption: Discovery Details
discovery_details.description: Details about the data discovered by classification job.

pattern_match.caption: Pattern Match
pattern_match.description: A text, binary, file name, or datastore that matched against a detection rule.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Details about the policy that triggered the finding.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The source URL pointing towards the full classification job details.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The resultant status of the classification job normalized to the caption of the status_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

status_details.caption: Status Details

reply_to_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header Reply To Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

return_path.caption: Return Path
return_path.description: The address found in the 'Return-Path' header, which indicates where bounce messages (non-delivery reports) should be sent. This address is often set by the sending system and may differ from the 'From' or 'Sender' addresses. For example, mailer-daemon@senderserver.com.

sender.caption: Sender
sender.description: The machine readable email address of the system or server that actually transmitted the email message, extracted from the email headers per RFC 5322. This differs from the from field, which shows the message author. The sender field is most commonly used when multiple addresses appear in the from_list field, or when the transmitting system is different from the message author (such as when sending on behalf of someone else).

sender_mailbox.caption: Sender Mailbox
sender_mailbox.description: The human readable email address of the system or server that actually transmitted the email message, extracted from the email headers per RFC 5322. This differs from the from_mailbox field, which shows the message author. The sender mailbox field is most commonly used when multiple addresses appear in the from_mailboxes field, or when the transmitting system is different from the message author (such as when sending on behalf of someone else).

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size in bytes of the email, including attachments.

smtp_from.caption: SMTP From
smtp_from.description: The value of the SMTP MAIL FROM command.

smtp_to.caption: SMTP To
smtp_to.description: The value of the SMTP envelope RCPT TO command.

subject.caption: Subject
subject.description: The email header Subject value, as defined by RFC 5322.

to.caption: To
to.description: The machine-readable email header To values, as defined by RFC 5322. For example example.user@usersdomain.com

to_mailboxes.caption: To Mailboxes
to_mailboxes.description: The human-readable email header To Mailbox values. For example 'Example User <example.user@usersdomain.com>'.

uid.caption: Email Thread UID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the email thread.

urls.caption: URLs
urls.description: The URLs embedded in the email.

x_originating_ip.caption: X-Originating-IP
x_originating_ip.description: The X-Originating-IP header identifying the emails originating IP address(es).

dkim.caption: DKIM Status
dkim.description: The DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) status of the email.

dkim_domain.caption: DKIM Domain
dkim_domain.description: The DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) signing domain of the email.

dkim_signature.caption: DKIM Signature
dkim_signature.description: The DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) signature used by the sending/receiving system.

dmarc.caption: DMARC Status
dmarc.description: The Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance (DMARC) status of the email.

dmarc_override.caption: DMARC Override
dmarc_override.description: The Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance (DMARC) override action.

dmarc_policy.caption: DMARC Policy
dmarc_policy.description: The Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance (DMARC) policy status.

spf.caption: SPF Status
spf.description: The Sender Policy Framework (SPF) status of the email.

algorithm.caption: Encryption Algorithm
algorithm.description: The encryption algorithm used, normalized to the caption of 'algorithm_id

key_length.caption: Encryption Key Length
key_length.description: The length of the encryption key used.

key_uid.caption: Key UID
key_uid.description: The unique identifier of the key used for encryption. For example, AWS KMS Key ARN.

type.caption: Encryption Type
type.description: The type of the encryption used.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

container.caption: Container
container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The name of the domain that the endpoint belongs to or that corresponds to the endpoint.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified name of the endpoint.

instance_uid.caption: Instance ID
instance_uid.description: The unique identifier of a VM instance.

interface_name.caption: Network Interface Name
interface_name.description: The name of the network interface (e.g. eth2).

interface_uid.caption: Network Interface ID
interface_uid.description: The unique identifier of the network interface.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the endpoint, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The geographical location of the endpoint.

mac.caption: MAC Address
mac.description: The Media Access Control (MAC) address of the endpoint.

mac_vendor.caption: MAC Vendor
mac_vendor.description: The vendor or manufacturer of the endpoint's network interface controller (NIC), as identified from the MAC address.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The short name of the endpoint.

namespace_pid.caption: Namespace PID
namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the endpoint or was last logged into it.

pool.caption: Pool
pool.description: The pool of desktops or virtual machines to which the endpoint belongs.

subnet_uid.caption: Subnet UID
subnet_uid.description: The unique identifier of a virtual subnet.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The endpoint type. For example: unknown, server, desktop, laptop, tablet, mobile, virtual, browser, or other.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The endpoint type ID.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the endpoint.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

vpc_uid.caption: VPC UID
vpc_uid.description: The unique identifier of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or LAN segment.

code.caption: Response Code
code.description: A numerical response status code providing details about the connection.

network_endpoint.caption: Network Endpoint
network_endpoint.description: Provides characteristics of the network endpoint.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the enrichment data was generated.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the enrichment data was generated.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The enrichment data associated with the attribute and value. The meaning of this data depends on the type the enrichment record.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A long description of the enrichment data.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the attribute to which the enriched data pertains.

reputation.caption: Reputation Scores
reputation.description: The reputation of the enrichment data.

short_desc.caption: Short Description
short_desc.description: A short description of the enrichment data.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The URL of the source of the enrichment data.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The enrichment type. For example: location.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The value of the attribute to which the enriched data pertains.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the environment variable.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The value of the environment variable.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the EPSS score was calculated.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The timestamp indicating when the EPSS score was calculated.

percentile.caption: EPSS Percentile
percentile.description: The EPSS score's percentile representing relative importance and ranking of the score in the larger EPSS dataset.

score.caption: EPPS Score
score.description: The EPSS score representing the probability [0-1] of exploitation in the wild in the next 30 days (following score publication).

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the EPSS model used to calculate the score.

actor.caption: Actor
actor.description: Describes details about the user/role/process that was the source of the activity that triggered the detection.

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: Describes details about an AI agent associated with the activity that triggered the detection, whether the agent performed the activity, was its target, or was otherwise involved. Use a separate evidences entry per agent when a finding involves more than one, such as an agent spawning a sub-agent in violation of usage policy.

api.caption: API Details
api.description: Describes details about the API call associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

connection_info.caption: Connection Info
connection_info.description: Describes details about the network connection associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

container.caption: Container
container.description: Describes details about the container associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Additional evidence data that is not accounted for in the specific evidence attributes. Use only when absolutely necessary.

database.caption: Database
database.description: Describes details about the database associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

databucket.caption: Databucket
databucket.description: Describes details about the databucket associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

device.caption: Device
device.description: An addressable device, computer system or host associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

dst_endpoint.caption: Destination Endpoint
dst_endpoint.description: Describes details about the destination of the network activity that triggered the detection.

email.caption: Email
email.description: The email object associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

file.caption: File
file.description: Describes details about the file associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

http_request.caption: HTTP Request
http_request.description: Describes details about the http request associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

http_response.caption: HTTP Response
http_response.description: Describes details about the http response associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

ja4_fingerprint_list.caption: JA4+ Fingerprints
ja4_fingerprint_list.description: Describes details about the JA4+ fingerprints that triggered the detection.

job.caption: Job
job.description: Describes details about the scheduled job that was associated with the activity that triggered the detection.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The naming convention or type identifier of the evidence associated with the security detection. For example, the @odata.type from Microsoft Graph Alerts V2 or display_name from CrowdStrike Falcon Incident Behaviors.

process.caption: Process
process.description: Describes details about the process associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

query.caption: DNS Query
query.description: Describes details about the DNS query associated to the activity that triggered the detection.

reg_key.caption: Registry Key
reg_key.description: Describes details about the registry key that triggered the detection.

reg_value.caption: Registry Value
reg_value.description: Describes details about the registry value that triggered the detection.

resources.caption: Cloud Resources
resources.description: Describes details about the cloud resources directly related to activity that triggered the detection. For resources impacted by the detection, use Affected Resources at the top-level of the finding.

script.caption: Script
script.description: Describes details about the script that was associated with the activity that triggered the detection.

src_endpoint.caption: Source Endpoint
src_endpoint.description: Describes details about the source of the network activity that triggered the detection.

tls.caption: TLS
tls.description: Describes details about the Transport Layer Security (TLS) activity that triggered the detection.

uid.caption: Unique ID
