type.description: The type of network interface.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The network interface type identifier.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier for the network interface.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: The Autonomous System details associated with an IP address.

container.caption: Container
container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The name of the domain that the endpoint belongs to or that corresponds to the endpoint.

fingerprints.caption: Fingerprints
fingerprints.description: Fingerprints that identify the specific application implementation on this endpoint, such as Cisco NPF or HASSH.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified name of the endpoint.

instance_uid.caption: Instance ID
instance_uid.description: The unique identifier of a VM instance.

interface_name.caption: Network Interface Name
interface_name.description: The name of the network interface (e.g. eth2).

interface_uid.caption: Network Interface ID
interface_uid.description: The unique identifier of the network interface.

intermediate_ips.caption: Intermediate IP Addresses
intermediate_ips.description: The intermediate IP Addresses. For example, the IP addresses in the HTTP X-Forwarded-For header.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the endpoint, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

isp.caption: ISP Name
isp.description: The name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP).

mac.description: The Media Access Control (MAC) address of the endpoint.

mac_vendor.description: The vendor or manufacturer of the endpoint's network interface controller (NIC), as identified from the MAC address.

name.description: The short name of the endpoint.

namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

network_scope_id.description: The normalized identifier of the endpoint’s network scope. svc_name.caption: Service Name
svc_name.description: The service name in service-to-service connections. For example, AWS VPC logs the pkt-src-aws-service and pkt-dst-aws-service fields identify the connection is coming from or going to an AWS service.

type.description: The network endpoint type. For example: unknown, server, desktop, laptop, tablet, mobile, virtual, browser, or other.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The network endpoint type ID.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the endpoint.

uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

vpc_uid.caption: VPC UID
vpc_uid.description: The unique identifier of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or LAN segment.

bytes.caption: Total Bytes
bytes.description: The total number of bytes transferred in both directions (sum of bytes_in and bytes_out).

bytes_in.caption: Bytes In
bytes_in.description: The number of bytes sent from the destination to the source (inbound direction).

bytes_missed.caption: Bytes Missed
bytes_missed.description: The number of bytes that were missed during observation, typically due to packet loss or sampling limitations.

bytes_out.caption: Bytes Out
bytes_out.description: The number of bytes sent from the source to the destination (outbound direction).

chunks.caption: Chunks
chunks.description: The total number of chunks transferred in both directions (sum of chunks_in and chunks_out).

chunks_in.caption: Chunks In
chunks_in.description: The number of chunks sent from the destination to the source (inbound direction).

chunks_out.caption: Chunks Out
chunks_out.description: The number of chunks sent from the source to the destination (outbound direction).

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The end time of the observation or reporting period.

end_time_dt.caption: End Time
end_time_dt.description: The end time of the observation or reporting period.

packets.caption: Total Packets
packets.description: The total number of packets transferred in both directions (sum of packets_in and packets_out).

packets_in.caption: Packets In
packets_in.description: The number of packets sent from the destination to the source (inbound direction).

packets_out.caption: Packets Out
packets_out.description: The number of packets sent from the source to the destination (outbound direction).

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The start time of the observation or reporting period.

start_time_dt.caption: Start Time
start_time_dt.description: The start time of the observation or reporting period.

timespan.caption: Time Span
timespan.description: The time span object representing the duration of the observation or reporting period.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Additional data about the node stored as key-value pairs. Can include custom properties specific to the node.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A human-readable description of the node's purpose or meaning in the graph.

name.caption: Name
name.description: A human-readable name or label for the node. Should be descriptive and unique within the graph context.

type.caption: Type
type.description: Categorizes the node into a specific class or type. Useful for grouping and filtering nodes.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique string or numeric identifier that distinguishes this node from all others in the graph. Must be unique across all nodes.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the note was created.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the note was created.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the note was last modified.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The time when the note was last modified.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The user who created or last modified the note. Typically the same user that created the note can modify the note.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A short description of the comment, if applicable.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the note, if applicable.

event_uid.caption: Event UID
event_uid.description: The unique identifier (metadata.uid) of the source OCSF event from which this observable was extracted. This field enables linking observables back to their originating event data when observables are stored in a separate location or system.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The full name of the observable attribute. The name is a pointer/reference to an attribute within the OCSF event data. For example: file.name. Array attributes may be represented in one of three ways. For example: resources.uid, resources[].uid, resources[0].uid.

reputation.caption: Reputation Scores
reputation.description: Contains the original and normalized reputation scores.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The observable value type name.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The observable value type identifier.

type_uid.caption: Type ID
type_uid.description: The OCSF event type UID (type_uid) of the source event that this observable was extracted from. This field enables filtering and categorizing observables by their originating event type. For example: 300101 for Network Activity (class_uid 3001) with activity_id 1.

value.caption: Value
value.description:
The value associated with the observable attribute. The meaning of the value depends on the observable type.
If the name refers to a scalar attribute, then the value is the value of the attribute.
If the name refers to an object attribute, then the value is not populated.

count.caption: Count
count.description: Integer representing the total number of times this specific value/event was observed across all occurrences. Helps establish prevalence and patterns.

timespan.caption: Time Span
timespan.description: The time window when the value or event was first observed. It is used to analyze activity patterns, detect trends, or correlate events within a specific timeframe.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The specific value, event, indicator or data point that was observed and recorded. This is the core piece of information being tracked.

cell_name.caption: Cell Name
cell_name.description: The cell name/reference in a spreadsheet. e.g A2

column_name.caption: Column Name
column_name.description: The column name in a spreadsheet, where the information was discovered.

column_number.caption: Column Number
column_number.description: The column number in a spreadsheet or a plain text document, where the information was discovered.

end_line.caption: End Line
end_line.description: The line number of the last line of the file, where the information was discovered.

json_path.caption: JSON Path
json_path.description: The JSON path of the attribute in a json record, where the information was discovered

page_number.caption: Page Number
page_number.description: The page number in a document, where the information was discovered.

record_index_in_array.caption: Record Index in Array
record_index_in_array.description: The index of the record in the array of records, where the information was discovered. e.g. the index of a record in an array of JSON records in a file.

row_number.caption: Row Number
row_number.description: The row number in a spreadsheet, where the information was discovered.

start_line.caption: Start Line
start_line.description: The line number of the first line of the file, where the information was discovered.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the organization, Oracle Cloud Tenancy, Google Cloud Organization, or AWS Organization. For example, Widget, Inc. or the AWS Organization name .

ou_name.caption: Org Unit Name
ou_name.description: The name of an organizational unit, Google Cloud Folder, or AWS Org Unit. For example, the GCP Project Name , or Dev_Prod_OU .

ou_uid.caption: Org Unit ID
ou_uid.description: The unique identifier of an organizational unit, Google Cloud Folder, or AWS Org Unit. For example, an Oracle Cloud Tenancy ID , AWS OU ID , or GCP Folder ID .

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the organization, Oracle Cloud Tenancy, Google Cloud Organization, or AWS Organization. For example, an AWS Org ID or Oracle Cloud Domain ID .

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

country.caption: Country
country.description:
The operating system country code, as defined by the ISO 3166-1 standard (Alpha-2 code).

Note: The two letter country code should be capitalized. For example: US or CA.

cpe_name.caption: The product CPE identifier
cpe_name.description: The Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) name. For example: cpe:/a:apple:safari:16.2.

cpu_bits.caption: CPU Bits
cpu_bits.description: The cpu architecture, the number of bits used for addressing in memory. For example: 32 or 64.

edition.caption: OS Edition
edition.description: The operating system edition. For example: Professional.

kernel_release.caption: Kernel Release
kernel_release.description: The kernel release of the operating system. On Unix-based systems, this is determined from the uname -r command output, for example "5.15.0-122-generic".

lang.caption: Language
lang.description: The two letter lower case language codes, as defined by ISO 639-1. For example: en (English), de (German), or fr (French).

name.caption: Name
name.description: The operating system name.

sp_name.caption: OS Service Pack
sp_name.description: The name of the latest Service Pack.

sp_ver.caption: OS Service Pack Version
sp_ver.description: The version number of the latest Service Pack.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the operating system.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type identifier of the operating system.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the OS running on the device that originated the event. For example: "Windows 10", "OS X 10.7", or "iOS 9".

answers.caption: Related DNS Answers
answers.description: Any pertinent DNS answers information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: MITRE ATT&CK Tactics, Techniques, and/or Procedures (TTPs) pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: Any pertinent autonomous system information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

campaign.caption: Campaign
campaign.description: The campaign object describes details about the campaign that was the source of the activity.

category.caption: Category
category.description: Categorizes the threat indicator based on its functional or operational role.

comment.caption: Analyst Comments
comment.description: Analyst commentary or source commentary about an indicator or OSINT analysis.

confidence.caption: Confidence
confidence.description: The confidence of an indicator or analysis, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source or analyst.

confidence_id.caption: Confidence ID
confidence_id.description: The normalized identifier of the confidence level, reflecting the accuracy or pertinence of the OSINT indicator or analysis. A low confidence indicates that the collected information lacked sufficient detail or accuracy to fully qualify the indicator as malicious. When the value is 99 (Other), the confidence attribute must contain the source-specific label.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The timestamp when the indicator was initially created or identified.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The timestamp when the indicator was initially created or identified.

creator.caption: Creator
creator.description: The identifier of the user, system, or organization that contributed the indicator.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A detailed explanation of the indicator, including its context, purpose, and relevance.

detection_pattern.caption: Detection Pattern
detection_pattern.description: The specific detection pattern or signature associated with the indicator.

detection_pattern_type.caption: Detection Pattern
detection_pattern_type.description: The detection pattern type, normalized to the caption of the detection_pattern_type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

detection_pattern_type_id.caption: Detection Pattern Type ID
detection_pattern_type_id.description: Specifies the type of detection pattern used to identify the associated threat indicator.

email.caption: Related Email
email.description: Any email information pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

email_auth.caption: Related Email Authentication
email_auth.description: Any email authentication information pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

expiration_time.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time.description: The expiration date of the indicator, after which it is no longer considered reliable.

expiration_time_dt.caption: Expiration Time
expiration_time_dt.description: The expiration date of the indicator, after which it is no longer considered reliable.

external_uid.caption: External ID
external_uid.description: A unique identifier assigned by an external system for cross-referencing.

file.caption: Related File
file.description: Any pertinent file information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

intrusion_sets.caption: Intrusion Sets
intrusion_sets.description: A grouping of adversarial behaviors and resources believed to be associated with specific threat actors or campaigns. Intrusion sets often encompass multiple campaigns and are used to organize related activities under a common label.

kill_chain.caption: Kill Chain
kill_chain.description: Lockheed Martin Kill Chain Phases pertinent to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: Tags or keywords associated with the indicator to enhance searchability.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: Any pertinent geolocation information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

malware.caption: Malware
malware.description: A list of Malware objects, describing details about the identified malware.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The timestamp of the last modification or update to the indicator.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The timestamp of the last modification or update to the indicator.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name is a pointer/reference to an attribute within the OCSF event data. For example: file.name.

references.caption: References
references.description: Provides a reference to an external source of information related to the CTI being represented. This may include a URL, a document, or some other type of reference that provides additional context or information about the CTI.

related_analytics.caption: Related Analytics
related_analytics.description: Any analytics related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

reputation.caption: Reputation Scores
reputation.description: Related reputational analysis from third-party engines and analysts for a given indicator or OSINT analysis.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: A numerical representation of the threat indicator’s risk level.

script.caption: Related Script Data
script.description: Any pertinent script information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: Represents the severity level of the threat indicator, typically reflecting its potential impact or damage.

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description: The normalized severity level of the threat indicator, typically reflecting its potential impact or damage.

signatures.caption: Related Digital Signatures
signatures.description: Any digital signatures or hashes related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The source URL of an indicator or OSINT analysis, e.g., a URL back to a TIP, report, or otherwise.

subdomains.caption: Related Subdomains
subdomains.description: Any pertinent subdomain information - such as those generated by a Domain Generation Algorithm - related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

subnet.caption: Related Subnet
subnet.description: A CIDR or network block related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

threat_actor.caption: Threat Actor
threat_actor.description: A threat actor is an individual or group that conducts malicious cyber activities, often with financial, political, or ideological motives.

tlp.caption: Traffic Light Protocol
tlp.description: The Traffic Light Protocol (TLP) was created to facilitate greater sharing of potentially sensitive information and more effective collaboration. TLP provides a simple and intuitive schema for indicating with whom potentially sensitive information can be shared.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The OSINT indicator type.

type_id.caption: Indicator Type ID
type_id.description: The OSINT indicator type ID.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier for the OSINT object.

uploaded_time.caption: Uploaded Time
uploaded_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the associated indicator or intelligence was added to the system or repository.

uploaded_time_dt.caption: Uploaded Time
uploaded_time_dt.description: The timestamp indicating when the associated indicator or intelligence was added to the system or repository.

value.caption: Indicator
value.description: The actual indicator value in scope, e.g., a SHA-256 hash hexdigest or a domain name.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The vendor name of a tool which generates intelligence or provides indicators.

vulnerabilities.caption: Related Vulnerabilities
vulnerabilities.description: Any vulnerabilities related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

whois.caption: WHOIS
whois.description: Any pertinent WHOIS information related to an indicator or OSINT analysis.

architecture.caption: Architecture
architecture.description: Architecture is a shorthand name describing the type of computer hardware the packaged software is meant to run on.

cpe_name.caption: The product CPE identifier
cpe_name.description: The Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) name. For example: cpe:/a:apple:safari:16.2.

epoch.caption: Epoch
epoch.description: The software package epoch. Epoch is a way to define weighted dependencies based on version numbers.

hash.caption: Hash
hash.description: Cryptographic hash to identify the binary instance of a software component. This can include any component such file, package, or library.

license.caption: Software License
license.description: The software license applied to this package.

license_url.caption: Software License URL
license_url.description: The URL pointing to the license applied on package or software. This is typically a LICENSE.md file within a repository.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The software package name.

package_manager.caption: Package Manager
package_manager.description: The software packager manager utilized to manage a package on a system, e.g. npm, yum, dpkg etc.

package_manager_url.caption: Package Manager URL
package_manager_url.description: The URL of the package or library at the package manager, or the specific URL or URI of an internal package manager link such as AWS CodeArtifact or Artifactory.

purl.caption: Package URL
purl.description: A purl is a URL string used to identify and locate a software package in a mostly universal and uniform way across programming languages, package managers, packaging conventions, tools, APIs and databases.

release.caption: Software Release Details
release.description: Release is the number of times a version of the software has been packaged.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The link to the specific library or package such as within GitHub, this is different from the link to the package manager where the library or package is hosted.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of software package, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type of software package.

uid.caption: Package UID
uid.description: A unique identifier for the package or library reported by the source tool. E.g., the libId within the sbom field of an OX Security Issue or the SPDX components.*.bom-ref.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor who published the software package.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The software package version.

encoding.caption: Encoding
encoding.description: The human-readable name of the encoding used to represent the packet data in the value field. This should match the caption associated with encoding_id. If encoding_id is 99 (Other), this field contains the original data source–specific encoding value.

encoding_id.caption: Encoding ID
encoding_id.description: The normalized identifier of the encoding method used to represent the packet data as a string.

end_offset.caption: End Offset
end_offset.description: The ending byte position of this packet within a capture file or stream.

format.caption: Format
format.description: The human-readable name of the packet capture file format in which the packet is stored. This should match the caption associated with format_id. If format_id is 99 (Other), this field contains the original data source–specific format value.

format_id.caption: Format ID
format_id.description: The normalized identifier of the packet capture format.

sequence_number.caption: Sequence Number
sequence_number.description: The relative order number of this packet within its capture context (such as a PCAP file, network session, or reconstructed stream). This represents chronological capture order, distinct from both protocol-level sequencing (such as TCP sequence numbers).

source.caption: Source
source.description: The human-readable name describing how or where the packet was obtained. This should match the caption associated with source_id. If source_id is 99 (Other), this field contains the original data source–specific value.

source_id.caption: Source ID
source_id.description: A normalized numeric identifier that specifies how the packet was obtained or generated.

start_offset.caption: Start Offset
start_offset.description: The starting byte position of this packet within a capture file or stream.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The actual packet data, represented as a string. The format of this string is determined by the specified encoding_id (e.g., Base64, Hexadecimal, or URL Encoded).

name.caption: Name
name.description: The parameter name.

post_value.caption: Post-Value
post_value.description: The parameter value after function execution.

pre_value.caption: Pre-Value
pre_value.description: The parameter value before function execution.

class.caption: Class
class.description: The class of the peripheral device.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the peripheral device.

type.caption: Peripheral Device Type
type.description: The Peripheral Device type, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

type_id.caption: Peripheral Device Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized peripheral device type ID.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the peripheral device.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

vendor_id_list.caption: Vendor ID List
vendor_id_list.description: The list of vendor IDs for the peripheral device.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The primary vendor name for the peripheral device.

analyzed_privileges_count.caption: Analyzed Privileges Count
analyzed_privileges_count.description: The total count of privileges that were analyzed across all services.

condition_keys.caption: Condition Keys
condition_keys.description: The condition keys and their values that were evaluated during policy analysis, including contextual constraints that affect permission grants. These conditions define when and how permissions are applied. Examples: aws:SourceIp:1.2.3.4, aws:RequestedRegion:us-east-1.

granted_privileges.caption: Granted Privileges
granted_privileges.description: The specific privileges, actions, or permissions that are explicitly granted by the analyzed policy. Examples: AWS actions like s3:GetObject, ec2:RunInstances, iam:CreateUser; Azure actions like Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/read; or GCP permissions like storage.objects.get.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Detailed information about the policy document that was analyzed, including policy metadata, version, type (identity-based, resource-based, etc.), and structural details. This provides context for understanding the scope and nature of the permission analysis.

service_privilege_analysis_list.caption: Service Privilege Analysis List
service_privilege_analysis_list.description: The list of privilege analysis results grouped by cloud service or namespace.

total_potential_attacks_count.caption: Total Potential Attacks Count
total_potential_attacks_count.description: The total count of privilege-to-attack technique mappings identified across all analyzed privileges.

unused_privileges_count.caption: Unused Privileges Count
unused_privileges_count.description: The total count of privileges or actions defined in the policy that have not been utilized within the analysis timeframe. This metric helps identify over-privileged access and opportunities for privilege reduction to follow the principle of least privilege. High counts may indicate policy bloat or excessive permissions.

unused_services_count.caption: Unused Services Count
unused_services_count.description: The total count of cloud services or resource types referenced in the policy that have not been accessed or utilized within the analysis timeframe. This helps identify unused service permissions that could be removed to reduce attack surface. Examples: AWS services like S3, SQS, IAM, Lambda; Azure services like Storage, Compute, KeyVault; or GCP services like Cloud Storage, Compute Engine, BigQuery.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Additional data about the policy such as the underlying JSON policy itself or other details.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the policy.

is_applied.caption: Applied
is_applied.description: A determination if the content of a policy was applied to a target or request, or not.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The policy name. For example: AdministratorAccess Policy.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The policy type. For example: Identity Policy, Resource Policy, Service Control Policy, etc..

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier of the policy instance.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The policy version number.

protocol_name.caption: Protocol Name
protocol_name.description: The IP protocol name in lowercase, as defined by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). For example: tcp or udp.

protocol_num.caption: Protocol Number
protocol_num.description: The IP protocol number, as defined by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA). For example: 6 for TCP and 17 for UDP.

fingerprint.caption: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the previous event, binding this reference to the previous event's content so that altering or substituting the previous event breaks the link. Refer to specific usage.

type_uid.caption: Type ID
type_uid.description: The event type identifier of the previous event, as carried in that event's type_uid. It directs a consumer to the event class, and therefore the table or store, where the previous event resides.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the previous event, as carried in that event's metadata.uid.

attack.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® Details
attack.description: The MITRE ATT&CK technique that these privileges could enable.

privilege_info_list.caption: Privilege Info List
privilege_info_list.description: The list of privilege information objects, where each element describes a specific privilege that could enable the associated attack technique.

is_unused.caption: Is Unused
is_unused.description: Indicates whether the privilege is unused within the analysis timeframe.

last_used_time.caption: Last Used Time
last_used_time.description: The most recent time this privilege was used.

last_used_time_dt.caption: Last Used Time
last_used_time_dt.description: The most recent time this privilege was used.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the privilege, action, or permission. Examples: GetObject, CreateStoreImageTask (AWS); Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/read (Azure); storage.objects.get (GCP).

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type or category of the privilege, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized type of the privilege.

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: The autonomous AI agent that this process is running or hosting, if applicable. Populate when the process serves as the runtime environment for an AI agent (e.g., a Python process executing a LangChain agent or hosting an MCP server). When a process hosts multiple agents and the activity cannot be attributed to one specifically, use hosted_ai_agent_list instead.

ancestry.caption: Ancestry
ancestry.description: An array of Process Entities describing the extended parentage of this process object. Direct parent information should be expressed through the parent_process attribute. The first array element is the direct parent of this process object. Subsequent list elements go up the process parentage hierarchy. That is, the array is sorted from newest to oldest process. It is recommended to only populate this field for the top-level process object.

auid.caption: Audit User ID
auid.description: The audit user assigned at login by the audit subsystem.

cmd_line.caption: Command Line
cmd_line.description: The full command line used to launch an application, service, process, or job. For example: ssh user@10.0.0.10. If the command line is unavailable or missing, the empty string '' is to be used.

container.caption: Container
container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

cpid.caption: Common Process Identifier
cpid.description: A unique process identifier that can be assigned deterministically by multiple system data producers.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the process was created/started.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the process was created/started.

egid.caption: Effective Group ID
egid.description: The effective group under which this process is running.

environment_variables.caption: Environment Variables
environment_variables.description: Environment variables associated with the process.

euid.caption: Effective User ID
euid.description: The effective user under which this process is running.

file.caption: File
file.description: The process file object.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The group under which this process is running.

hosted_ai_agent_list.caption: Hosted AI Agent List
hosted_ai_agent_list.description: The list of autonomous AI agents hosted by this process. Use when a single process hosts multiple agents (e.g., an IDE running several coding agents within the same host process) and the producer cannot attribute a specific activity to a single agent. When attribution is available, populate the singular ai_agent attribute instead.

hosted_services.caption: Hosted Services
hosted_services.description: The Windows services that this process is hosting.

integrity.caption: Integrity
integrity.description: The process integrity level, normalized to the caption of the integrity_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source (Windows only).

integrity_id.caption: Integrity Level
integrity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the process integrity level (Windows only).

lineage.caption: Lineage
lineage.description: The lineage of the process, represented by a list of paths for each ancestor process. For example: ['/usr/sbin/sshd', '/usr/bin/bash', '/usr/bin/whoami'].

loaded_modules.caption: Loaded Modules
loaded_modules.description: The list of loaded module names.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The friendly name of the process, for example: Notepad++.

namespace_pid.caption: Namespace PID
namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

parent_process.caption: Parent Process
parent_process.description: The parent process of this process object. It is recommended to only populate this field for the top-level process object, to prevent deep nesting. Additional ancestry information can be supplied in the ancestry attribute.

pid.caption: Process ID
pid.description: The process identifier, as reported by the operating system. Process ID (PID) is a number used by the operating system to uniquely identify an active process.

ptid.caption: Process Thread ID
ptid.description: The identifier of the process thread associated with the event, as returned by the operating system.

sandbox.caption: Sandbox
sandbox.description: The name of the containment jail (i.e., sandbox). For example, hardened_ps, high_security_ps, oracle_ps, netsvcs_ps, or default_ps.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The user session under which this process is running.

terminated_time.caption: Terminated Time
terminated_time.description: The time when the process was terminated.

terminated_time_dt.caption: Terminated Time
terminated_time_dt.description: The time when the process was terminated.

tid.caption: Thread ID
tid.description: The identifier of the thread associated with the event, as returned by the operating system.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for this process assigned by the producer (tool).  Facilitates correlation of a process event with other events for that process.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user under which this process is running.

working_directory.caption: Working Directory
working_directory.description: The working directory of a process.

xattributes.caption: Extended Attributes
xattributes.description:
An unordered collection of zero or more name/value pairs that represent a process extended attribute.

For example: process security context attributes, process resource limits, container-specific attributes, or platform-specific process metadata not covered by standard OCSF attributes.

cmd_line.caption: Command Line
cmd_line.description: The full command line used to launch an application, service, process, or job. For example: ssh user@10.0.0.10. If the command line is unavailable or missing, the empty string '' is to be used.

cpid.caption: Common Process Identifier
cpid.description: A unique process identifier that can be assigned deterministically by multiple system data producers.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the process was created/started.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the process was created/started.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The friendly name of the process, for example: Notepad++.

pid.caption: Process ID
pid.description: The process identifier, as reported by the operating system. Process ID (PID) is a number used by the operating system to uniquely identify an active process.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for this process assigned by the producer (tool).  Facilitates correlation of a process event with other events for that process.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

cpe_name.caption: The product CPE identifier
cpe_name.description: The Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) name. For example: cpe:/a:apple:safari:16.2.

data_classification.caption: Data Classification
data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.caption: Data Classification
data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

feature.caption: Feature
feature.description: The feature that reported the event.

lang.caption: Language
lang.description: The two letter lower case language codes, as defined by ISO 639-1. For example: en (English), de (German), or fr (French).

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the product.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The installation path of the product.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the product.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

url_string.caption: URL String
url_string.description: The URL pointing towards the product.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor of the product.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the product, as defined by the event source. For example: 2013.1.3-beta.

last_used_time.caption: Last Used Time
last_used_time.description: The timestamp when this programmatic credential was last used for authentication or API access. This helps track credential usage patterns, identify dormant credentials that may pose security risks, and support credential lifecycle management. The timestamp should reflect the most recent successful authentication or API call using this credential.

last_used_time_dt.caption: Last Used Time
last_used_time_dt.description: The timestamp when this programmatic credential was last used for authentication or API access. This helps track credential usage patterns, identify dormant credentials that may pose security risks, and support credential lifecycle management. The timestamp should reflect the most recent successful authentication or API call using this credential.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type or category of programmatic credential, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source. Examples include 'API Key', 'Service Account Key', 'Access Token', 'Client Certificate', 'OAuth Token', 'Personal Access Token', etc.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the programmatic credential. This could be an API key ID, service account key ID, access token identifier, certificate serial number, or other unique identifier that distinguishes this credential from others. Examples: AWS Access Key ID, GCP Service Account Key ID, Azure Application ID, or OAuth2 token identifier.

connection_info.caption: Connection Info
connection_info.description: The network connection information related to a Network Connection query type.

file.caption: File
file.description: The file that is the target of the query when query_type_id indicates a File query.

folder.caption: Folder
folder.description: The folder that is the target of the query when query_type_id indicates a Folder query.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The administrative group that is the target of the query when query_type_id indicates an Admin Group query.

job.caption: Job
job.description: The job object that pertains to the event when query_type_id indicates a Job query.

kernel.caption: Kernel
kernel.description: The kernel object that pertains to the event when query_type_id indicates a Kernel query.

module.caption: Module
module.description: The module that pertains to the event when query_type_id indicates a Module query.

network_interfaces.caption: Network Interfaces
network_interfaces.description: The physical or virtual network interfaces that are associated with the device when query_type_id indicates a Network Interfaces query.

peripheral_device.caption: Peripheral Device
peripheral_device.description: The peripheral device that triggered the event when query_type_id indicates a Peripheral Device query.

process.caption: Process
process.description: The process that pertains to the event when query_type_id indicates a Process query.

query_type.caption: Query Type
query_type.description: The normalized caption of query_type_id or the source-specific query type.

query_type_id.caption: Query Type ID
query_type_id.description: The normalized type of system query performed against a device or system component.

reg_key.caption: Registry Key
reg_key.description: The registry key object describes a Windows registry key.

reg_value.caption: Registry Value
reg_value.description: The registry value object describes a Windows registry value.

service.caption: Service
service.description: The service that pertains to the event when query_type_id indicates a Service query.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The authenticated user or service session when query_type_id indicates a Session query.

startup_item.caption: Startup Item
startup_item.description: The startup item object that pertains to the event when query_type_id indicates a Startup Item query.

state.caption: Network Connection State
state.description: The state of the socket, normalized to the caption of the state_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

tcp_state_id.caption: TCP State ID
tcp_state_id.description: The state of the TCP socket for the network connection.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user that pertains to the event when query_type_id indicates a User query.

users.caption: Users
users.description: The users that belong to the administrative group when query_type_id indicates a Users query.

bytes.caption: Total Bytes
bytes.description: The size of the data returned from the query.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The data returned from the query execution.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The query name for a saved or scheduled query.

query_string.caption: Query String
query_string.description: A string representing the query code being run. For example: SELECT * FROM my_table

query_time.caption: Query Time
query_time.description: The time when the query was run.

query_time_dt.caption: Query Time
query_time_dt.description: The time when the query was run.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the query.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

count.caption: Count
count.description: The number of times that activity in the same logical group occurred, as reported by the related Finding.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description:
The time when the related event/finding was created.

If the related event/finding is in OCSF and is a Finding, then this value should be equal to finding_info.created_time in the corresponding Finding. If the related event/finding is in OCSF and is not a Finding, then this value should be equal to time in the corresponding event.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description:
The time when the related event/finding was created.

If the related event/finding is in OCSF and is a Finding, then this value should be equal to finding_info.created_time in the corresponding Finding. If the related event/finding is in OCSF and is not a Finding, then this value should be equal to time in the corresponding event.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A description of the related event/finding.

first_seen_time.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time.description:
The time when the finding was first observed. e.g. The time when a vulnerability was first observed.
It can differ from the created_time timestamp, which reflects the time this finding was created.

first_seen_time_dt.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time_dt.description:
The time when the finding was first observed. e.g. The time when a vulnerability was first observed.
It can differ from the created_time timestamp, which reflects the time this finding was created.

kill_chain.caption: Kill Chain
kill_chain.description: The Kill Chain provides a detailed description of each phase and its associated activities within the broader context of a cyber attack.

last_seen_time.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time.description:
The time when the finding was most recently observed. e.g. The time when a vulnerability was most recently observed.
It can differ from the modified_time timestamp, which reflects the time this finding was last modified.

last_seen_time_dt.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time_dt.description:
The time when the finding was most recently observed. e.g. The time when a vulnerability was most recently observed.
It can differ from the modified_time timestamp, which reflects the time this finding was last modified.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the related event/finding was last modified.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The time when the related event/finding was last modified.

observables.caption: Observables
observables.description: The observables array surfaces key indicators and entities from the event or finding in a single, consistent location for downstream correlation and detection. Each entry references an attribute path within the event (e.g., src_endpoint.ip) along with its type and value, enabling consumers to extract IOCs without parsing the full event structure.

product.caption: Product
product.description: Details about the product that reported the related event/finding.

product_uid.caption: Product Identifier
product_uid.description: The unique identifier of the product that reported the related event.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. For all other values, this should match the caption defined for that severity_id enum value (e.g., "High" for severity_id: 4).

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity.

The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. Smaller numerical values represent lower impact events, and larger numerical values represent higher impact events.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The related event status. Should correspond to the label of the status_id (or 'Other' status value for status_id = 99) of the related event.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated with the related event/finding.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the related event/finding.

traits.caption: Traits
traits.description: The list of key traits or characteristics extracted from the related event/finding that influenced or contributed to the overall finding's outcome.

type.caption: Type
type.description:
The type of the related event/finding.

Populate if the related event/finding is NOT in OCSF. If it is in OCSF, then utilize type_name, type_uid instead.

type_name.caption: Type Name
type_name.description:
The type of the related OCSF event, as defined by type_uid.

For example: Process Activity: Launch.

Populate if the related event/finding is in OCSF.

type_uid.caption: Type ID
type_uid.description:
The unique identifier of the related OCSF event type.

For example: 100701.

Populate if the related event/finding is in OCSF.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description:
The unique identifier of the related event/finding.

If the related event/finding is in OCSF, then this value must be equal to metadata.uid in the corresponding event.

cis_controls.caption: CIS Controls
cis_controls.description: An array of Center for Internet Security (CIS) Controls that can be optionally mapped to provide additional remediation details.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the remediation strategy.

kb_article_list.caption: Knowledgebase Articles
kb_article_list.description: A list of KB articles or patches related to an endpoint. A KB Article contains metadata that describes the patch or an update.

kb_articles.caption: Knowledgebase Articles
kb_articles.description: The KB article/s related to the entity. A KB Article contains metadata that describes the patch or an update.

references.caption: References
references.description: A list of supporting URL/s, references that help describe the remediation strategy.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The hostname of the entity from which the event or finding was reported.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the entity from which the event or finding was reported.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the entity from which the event or finding was reported.

org.caption: Organization
org.description: The organization properties of the entity that reported the event or finding.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the entity from which the event or finding was reported.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

base_score.caption: Reputation Score
base_score.description: The reputation score as reported by the event source.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The provider of the reputation information.

score.caption: Reputation Score
score.description: The reputation score, normalized to the caption of the score_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

containers.caption: Containers
containers.description: When working with containerized applications, the set of containers which write to the standard the output of a particular logging driver. For example, this may be the set of containers involved in handling api requests and responses for a containerized application.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The additional data that is associated with the api request.

flags.caption: Flags
flags.description: The communication flags that are associated with the api request.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique request identifier.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

cloud_partition.caption: Cloud Partition
cloud_partition.description: The logical grouping or isolated segment within a cloud provider's infrastructure where the resource is located. Examples include AWS partitions (aws, aws-cn, aws-us-gov), Azure cloud environments (AzureCloud, AzureUSGovernment, AzureChinaCloud), or similar logical divisions in other cloud providers.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the resource was created.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the resource was created.

criticality.caption: Criticality
criticality.description:
Criticality or relative importance of this resource, normalized to the caption of criticality_id. In the case of Other, the value is defined by the event source.

Note: For versions prior to 1.9, criticality_id was not available and this is a source specific value.

criticality_id.caption: Criticality Level ID
criticality_id.description: The normalized identifier for the criticality or relative importance of this resource. Select the value that best reflects the operational and security impact if the resource were compromised or made unavailable. See the criticality sibling attribute for the corresponding human-readable label.

data_classification.caption: Data Classification
data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.caption: Data Classification
data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

device.caption: Device
device.description: The device details when the resource type is a device — for example, a cloud compute instance, a laptop, or a network appliance. Provides structured device attributes (OS, type, hardware, agent) that the resource's scalar fields cannot represent — beyond what the hostname and ip attributes capture. The device.name and device.uid should match the name and uid of this objects; the device.hostname value should match the hostname attribute of this object. The top-level hostname and ip remain the primary identifiers for the device resource.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The name of the related resource group.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified name of the resource. If the resource is a device, this should match device.hostname.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the resource, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format. If the resource is a device, this should match device.ip.

is_backed_up.caption: Back Ups Configured
is_backed_up.description: Indicates whether the device or resource has a backup enabled, such as an automated snapshot or a cloud backup. For example, this is indicated by the cloudBackupEnabled value within JAMF Pro mobile devices or the registration of an AWS ARN with the AWS Backup service.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the resource.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the resource was last modified.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The time when the resource was last modified.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the resource.

namespace.caption: Namespace
namespace.description: The namespace is useful when similar entities exist that you need to keep separate.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The details of the entity that owns the resource. Usually not the same as user that may not own the resource. For example the owner of the directory server but not a user in the directory. This object includes properties such as the owner's name, unique identifier, type, domain, and other relevant attributes that help identify the resource owner within the environment.

provider.caption: Cloud Provider
provider.description: The cloud service provider that hosts or manages the resource. This field is typically used when the resource is managed by a different provider than the one generating the event or finding. Examples include AWS, Azure, GCP (Google Cloud Platform), Oracle Cloud, IBM Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, or other public, private, or hybrid cloud providers.

region.caption: Region
region.description: The cloud region where the resource is hosted, as defined by the cloud provider. This represents the physical or logical geographic area containing the infrastructure supporting the resource. Examples include AWS regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1), Azure regions (East US, West Europe), GCP regions (us-central1, europe-west1), or Oracle Cloud regions (us-ashburn-1, uk-london-1).

resource_relationship.caption: Resource Relationship
resource_relationship.description: A graph representation showing how this resource relates to and interacts with other entities in the environment. This can include parent/child relationships, dependencies, or other connections.

role.caption: Role
role.description: The role of the resource in the context of the event or finding, normalized to the caption of the role_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

role_id.caption: Role ID
role_id.description: The normalized identifier of the resource's role in the context of the event or finding.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the resource.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The resource type as defined by the event source.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the resource.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternative unique identifier of the resource.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user represented by this resource — for example, a cloud IAM user, a local account, or an application identity. Provides structured user attributes (email, groups, privileges) that this object's scalar fields such as name cannot represent. Distinct from owner, which identifies the entity responsible for managing the resource. The user.name value should match the name attribute of this object, user.uid should match the uid of this object.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the resource. For example 1.2.3.

zone.caption: Cloud Availability Zone
zone.description: The availability zone within a cloud region where the resource is located. Examples include AWS availability zones (us-east-1a, us-east-1b), Azure availability zones (1, 2, 3 within a region), GCP zones (us-central1-a, us-central1-b), or Oracle Cloud availability domains (AD-1, AD-2, AD-3).

code.caption: Response Code
code.description: The numeric response sent to a request.

containers.caption: Containers
containers.description: When working with containerized applications, the set of containers which write to the standard the output of a particular logging driver. For example, this may be the set of containers involved in handling api requests and responses for a containerized application.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The additional data that is associated with the api response.

flags.caption: Flags
flags.description: The communication flags that are associated with the api response.

message.caption: Message
message.description: The response message provided by the service or API.

ack_reason.caption: Acknowledgement Reason
ack_reason.description: An integer that provides a reason code or additional information about the acknowledgment result.

ack_result.caption: Acknowledgement Result
ack_result.description: An integer that denotes the acknowledgment result of the DCE/RPC call.

uuid.caption: UUID
uuid.description: The unique identifier of the particular remote procedure or service.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the DCE/RPC protocol being used in the session.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the rule that generated the event.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the rule that generated the event.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The rule type.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the rule that generated the event.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The rule version. For example: 1.1.

name.caption: Name
name.description: Name of SAN (e.g. The actual IP Address or domain.)

type.caption: Type
type.description: Type descriptor of SAN (e.g. IP Address/domain/etc.)

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the SBOM was created.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the SBOM was created.

package.caption: Software Package
package.description: The software package or library that is being discovered or inventoried by an SBOM.

product.caption: Product
product.description: Details about the upstream product that generated the SBOM e.g. cdxgen or Syft.

software_components.caption: Software Components
software_components.description: The list of software components used in the software package.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of SBOM, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type of SBOM.

uid.caption: SBOM ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for the SBOM or the SBOM generation by a source tool, such as the SPDX metadata.component.bom-ref.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The specification (spec) version of the particular SBOM, e.g., 1.6.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The administrator-supplied or application-generated name of the scan. For example: "Home office weekly user database scan", "Scan folders for viruses", "Full system virus scan"

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of scan.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type id of the scan.

uid.caption: Scan UID
uid.description: The application-defined unique identifier assigned to an instance of a scan.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

auth_protocol.caption: Auth Protocol
auth_protocol.description: The authorization protocol as defined by the caption of auth_protocol_id. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

auth_protocol_id.caption: Auth Protocol ID
auth_protocol_id.description: The normalized identifier of the authorization protocol used by the SCIM resource.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: When the SCIM resource was added to the service provider.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: When the SCIM resource was added to the service provider.

error_message.caption: Last Error Message
error_message.description: Message or code associated with the last encountered error.

is_group_provisioning_enabled.caption: SCIM Group Provisioning Enabled
is_group_provisioning_enabled.description: Indicates whether the SCIM resource is configured to provision groups, automatically or otherwise.

is_user_provisioning_enabled.caption: SCIM User Provisioning Enabled
is_user_provisioning_enabled.description: Indicates whether the SCIM resource is configured to provision users, automatically or otherwise.

last_run_time.caption: Last Sync Time
last_run_time.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful synchronization.

last_run_time_dt.caption: Last Sync Time
last_run_time_dt.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful synchronization.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The most recent time when the SCIM resource was updated at the service provider.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The most recent time when the SCIM resource was updated at the service provider.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the SCIM resource.

protocol_name.caption: Supported Protocol
protocol_name.description: The supported protocol for the SCIM resource. E.g., SAML, OIDC, or OAuth2.

rate_limit.caption: Rate Limit
rate_limit.description: Maximum number of requests allowed by the SCIM resource within a specified time frame to avoid throttling.

scim_group_schema.caption: SCIM Group Schema
scim_group_schema.description: SCIM provides a schema for representing groups, identified using the following schema URI: urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group as defined in RFC 7634. This attribute will capture key-value pairs for the scheme implemented in a SCIM resource.

scim_user_schema.caption: SCIM User Schema
scim_user_schema.description: SCIM provides a resource type for user resources. The core schema for user is identified using the following schema URI: urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User as defined in RFC 7634. This attribute will capture key-value pairs for the scheme implemented in a SCIM resource. This object is inclusive of both the basic and Enterprise User Schema Extension.

state.caption: State
state.description: The provisioning state of the SCIM resource, normalized to the caption of the state_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

state_id.caption: State ID
state_id.description: The normalized state ID of the SCIM resource to reflect its activation status.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for a SCIM resource as defined by the service provider.

uid_alt.caption: External ID
uid_alt.description: A String that is an identifier for the resource as defined by the provisioning client. The externalId may simplify identification of a resource between the provisioning client and the service provider by allowing the client to use a filter to locate the resource with an identifier from the provisioning domain, obviating the need to store a local mapping between the provisioning domain's identifier of the resource and the identifier used by the service provider.

url_string.caption: SCIM Endpoint URL
url_string.description: The primary URL for SCIM API requests.

vendor_name.caption: Service Provider
vendor_name.description: Name of the vendor or service provider implementing SCIM. E.g., Okta, Auth0, Microsoft.

version.caption: SCIM Version
version.description: SCIM protocol version supported e.g., SCIM 2.0.

file.caption: File
file.description: Present if this script is associated with a file. Not present in the case of a file-less script.

hashes.caption: Hashes
hashes.description: An array of the script's cryptographic hashes. Note that these hashes are calculated on the script in its original encoding, and not on the normalized UTF-8 encoding found in the script_content attribute.

name.caption: Name
name.description: Unique identifier for the script or macro, independent of the containing file, used for tracking, auditing, and security analysis.

parent_uid.caption: Parent Unique ID
parent_uid.description: This attribute relates a sub-script to a parent script having the matching uid attribute. In the case of PowerShell, sub-script execution can be identified by matching the activity correlation ID of the raw ETW events provided by the OS.

script_content.caption: Script Content

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The end timestamp of the span, essential for identifying latency and performance bottlenecks. Like the start time, this timestamp is normalized across the observability system to ensure consistency, even when events are recorded across distributed services with unsynchronized clocks. Normalized time allows for accurate duration calculations and helps observability tools track performance across services, regardless of the individual system time settings.

end_time_dt.caption: End Time
end_time_dt.description: The end timestamp of the span, essential for identifying latency and performance bottlenecks. Like the start time, this timestamp is normalized across the observability system to ensure consistency, even when events are recorded across distributed services with unsynchronized clocks. Normalized time allows for accurate duration calculations and helps observability tools track performance across services, regardless of the individual system time settings.

message.caption: Message
message.description: The message in a span (often referred to as a span event) serves as a way to record significant moments or occurrences during the span's lifecycle. This content typically manifests as log entries, annotations, or semi-structured events as a string, providing additional granularity and context about what happens at specific points during the execution of an operation.

operation.caption: Operation

parent_uid.caption: Parent Unique ID

service.caption: Service

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The start timestamp of the span, essential for identifying latency and performance bottlenecks. This timestamp is normalized across the observability system, ensuring consistency even when events occur across distributed services with potentially unsynchronized clocks. By using normalized time, observability tools can provide accurate, uniform measurements of operation performance and latency, regardless of where or when the events actually occur.

start_time_dt.caption: Start Time
start_time_dt.description: The start timestamp of the span, essential for identifying latency and performance bottlenecks. This timestamp is normalized across the observability system, ensuring consistency even when events occur across distributed services with potentially unsynchronized clocks. By using normalized time, observability tools can provide accurate, uniform measurements of operation performance and latency, regardless of where or when the events actually occur.

status_code.caption: Status Code
status_code.description: Indicates the outcome of the operation in the span, such as success, failure, or error. Issues in a span typically refer to problems such as failed operations, timeouts, service unavailability, or errors in processing that can negatively impact the performance or reliability of the system. Tracking the `status_code` helps pinpoint these issues, enabling quicker identification and resolution of system inefficiencies or faults.

duration.caption: Duration Milliseconds
duration.description: The total time, in milliseconds, that the trace covers, calculated as the difference between start_time and end_time. This duration helps assess the overall performance of a request as it travels across various services, and is essential for identifying latency and potential bottlenecks within the distributed system. The trace duration may differ from individual span durations due to the propagation and processing times of the trace as it spans multiple components.

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The end timestamp of the trace, essential for identifying latency and performance bottlenecks. Like the start time, this timestamp is normalized across the trace system to ensure consistency, even when events are recorded across distributed services with unsynchronized clocks. Normalized time allows for accurate trace duration calculations and helps observability tools track overall performance across services, regardless of the individual system time settings.

end_time_dt.caption: End Time
end_time_dt.description: The end timestamp of the trace, essential for identifying latency and performance bottlenecks. Like the start time, this timestamp is normalized across the trace system to ensure consistency, even when events are recorded across distributed services with unsynchronized clocks. Normalized time allows for accurate trace duration calculations and helps observability tools track overall performance across services, regardless of the individual system time settings.

flags.caption: Flags
flags.description: The flags associated with the trace, used to indicate specific properties or behaviors, such as whether the trace is sampled or if it has special handling. Flags help control how traces are processed, logged, and analyzed, providing valuable context for tracing and observability tools in identifying trace characteristics or specific tracking requirements.

service.caption: Service
service.description: Identifies the service or component generating the trace, helping to track and correlate the flow of requests through various parts of a distributed system. This information is essential for understanding the role and performance of specific services within the broader context of system operations and for diagnosing issues across different components.

span.caption: Span
span.description: Represents a single unit of work or operation within a distributed trace. A span typically tracks the execution of a request across a service, capturing important details such as the operation, timestamps, and status. Spans help break down the overall trace into smaller, manageable parts, enabling detailed analysis of the performance and behavior of specific operations within the system. They are crucial for understanding latency, dependencies, and bottlenecks in complex distributed systems.

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The start timestamp of the trace, essential for identifying latency and performance bottlenecks. Like the end time, this timestamp is normalized across the trace system to ensure consistency, even when events are recorded across distributed services with unsynchronized clocks. Normalized time enables accurate trace duration calculations and helps observability tools track performance across services, regardless of the individual system time settings.

start_time_dt.caption: Start Time
